main_topics.reason: The user came in overwhelmed by the two diagnoses and asked how they are connected and which came first.
The user asked why metformin was suggested despite not having diabetes and later chose to start it as their doctor advised.
The user asked what they could do beyond medication and engaged with discussion of movement and eating patterns.
The user said repeated efforts to lose weight had been frustrating and that PCOS made it feel almost impossible.
The user specifically asked whether metformin causes stomach problems.
The user asked whether there is a specific diet and whether lower-glycemic eating means eliminating carbohydrates.
The user asked what exercise is best and said they do not enjoy going to the gym.
The user asked whether a continuous glucose monitor might be useful for them.
The user briefly doubted their insurer would cover a monitor for this purpose.
The user described feeling overwhelmed by the new diagnosis and later said the explanation made it feel less scary.

output.summary: The user wanted to understand newly identified insulin resistance alongside PCOS and asked about metformin, side effects, lifestyle changes, diet, exercise, and a glucose monitor. The assistant explained these topics and acknowledged the user's frustration about weight loss; the user said the discussion helped and planned to start metformin as their doctor suggested and walk more after dinner.
